newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish publicans climb down on price of pint.
newsitem.headline: Irish publicans climb down on price of pint.

text.p: Dublin publicans agreed to reverse increases of up to five pence on a pint in an attempt to avoid a government-enforced price freeze.
The move followed a special meeting of the Licensed Vintners Association (LVA) held on Wednesday night.

"I welcome the decision by the Dublin Vintners to endorse the agreement I entered into last Thursday ... to restore pub prices to their early November levels," minister for Commerce, Science and Technology, Pat Rabbitte said in a statement following the decision by the LVA.
The decision will affect any price increases on stout beer, ale and lager as well as whiskey, gin and vodka.
Rabbitte had warned publicans on January 31 that if they did not drop their prices he would enforce a price-fixing order and freeze prices at their November 1996 level.
Concern over the recent price rises had prompted Ireland's Competition Authority to announce its intention to review the entire Irish drinks industry.
